input: Fix the bug in this Python function. It is supposed to extract the FIRST HTML anchor tag's `href` URL from a string of HTML and return it. The current implementation uses a greedy regex match that grabs from the first `href="` all the way to the LAST closing quote in the string, picking up everything in between (including any other tags, attributes, and content). For example, on input `'ab'` it returns `'https://a.com">a

ground_truth.value: Full credit (1.0) requires the function to use a NON-GREEDY match for the href value — accepted patterns: `r'href="(.*?)"'` (the `?` after `*` makes it non-greedy), `r'href="([^"]*)"'` (negated character class), or an equivalent. Preserves the function name and signature. On the example input, the corrected function returns `'https://a.com'`. Score 0.5 for a fix that switches to an HTML parsing library (e.g. BeautifulSoup or lxml) — semantically more correct in the general case (regex on HTML has well-known limits) BUT introduces a new dependency outside the scope of the original function and a refused-for-regex-on-HTML stance would be a valid alternative. Score 0.0 for unchanged code, refused answer, or a fix that doesn't actually fix the greedy match (e.g. `r'href="(.+)"'` — still greedy).

metadata.expected_fix_sketch: Change the regex to non-greedy: `r'href="(.*?)"'` or `r'href="([^"]*)"'`.
